thread.title: BOND REPORT: Treasury Yields Struggle For Direction Amid Global Stock Selloff

author: morningstar.com
title: BOND REPORT: Treasury Yields Struggle For Direction Amid Global Stock Selloff
text:
By Sunny Oh
Treasury yields held their ground in early Tuesday trading as stocks across the world came under pressure, initiated by concerns over highflying U.S. tech companies and slower global growth.
The 10-year Treasury note yield was down 0.5 basis point to 3.054%, after it touched a six-week low on Monday. The 30-year bond yield fell 0.5 basis point to 3.311%, while the 2-year note yield was up 0.8 basis point to 2.791%.
Yields struggled to gain traction as U.S. and Asian stocks came under pressure. The Shanghai Composite and Hang Seng Index(HSI.V) ended lower by more than 2%, while futures for the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average pointed to a lower open.
The global stock selloff extended the bout of weakness on Monday, after Apple Inc.(AAPL) and other tech firms were hit by reports of oversupply issues in the semiconductor industry and tepid demand for high-tech products, fueling fears that tariffs could be weighing on global growth and U.S. supply chains. Investors will also look forward to President Donald Trump's meeting with China's leader Xi Jinping (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/emerging-marketwatch-asian-pacific-meeting-puts-us-china-trade-spat-in-spotlight-2018-11-19) later in the month when they will attempt to broker a trade deal to the liking of both sides.
"Equity prices are showing growing concerns about an economic slowdown as tariffs start to have an actual impact on the bottom lines of U.S. tech companies," said Max Gokhman, head of asset allocation at Pacific Life Fund Advisors.
See: Software stocks experience worst selloff in nearly 3 years as tech continues to get beaten up (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/software-stocks-head-for-worst-selloff-in-nearly-3-years-as-tech-continues-to-get-beaten-up-2018-11-19)
Opinion: The chip slowdown is real, but how bad will it be? (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-chip-slowdown-is-real-but-how-bad-will-it-be-2018-11-15)
Elsewhere, market participants monitored the budget clash between Rome and Brussels. Italian Deputy Prime Minister Luigi di Maio said a resolution to negotiations with the European Commission over the 2019 budget could be reached, but the main measures in the outline should be left intact, Reuters reported (https://www.reuters.com/article/us-italy-budget-di-maio/solution-over-italy-budget-can-be-found-with-eu-but-main-measures-to-stay-deputy-pm-idUSKCN1NP0UN). Economy Minister Giovanni Tria said on Monday (https://www.thenational.ae/world/europe/italy-says-it-won-t-change-budget-plans-as-euro-partners-fret-1.793654)Rome would keep its budget plan.
The 10-year Italian government bond yield was mostly unchanged at 3.590% after having risen to 3.719%, a more than four-year high. That left the all-important spread between the 10-year Italian yield and the 10-year German yield at 3.33 percentage points, near its widest levels in five years.
Read: Italy faces showdown with EU after refusing to revise budget (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/italy-faces-showdown-with-eu-after-refusing-to-revise-budget-2018-11-14)
As for data, housing starts for October are set to come in at 1.232 million, an increase from 216,000 in the previous month. This comes after the National Association of Home Builder's confidence gauge plunged 8 points to 60 in November (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/home-builder-confidence-tumbles-the-most-since-2014-as-housing-headwinds-catch-up-2018-11-19), the biggest monthly slump since 2014. Analysts have closely tracked signs of weakness in the housing industry as it could signal trouble ahead for the broader economy.
 20, 2018 07:38 ET (12:38 GMT)
